text:
maya: Quick q — our current sampler is causing weird quota spikes when /v1/chat has short high-volume bursts. It's set to a flat per-route rate and we keep burning inspect credits during nightly spikes. any ideas? :thinking_face:

sam: Are you talking request-level sampling or token-level? I think chat routes are heavy on tokens so per-request % might not reflect cost.

maya: request-level. e.g. 5% of requests for /v1/chat is fine normally but if a tenant sends 10k small messages in a minute we end up sampling 500 requests → inspect quota meltdown.

jules: Could we add a burst_protection layer that caps samples per-window per-route and then uses EWMA of token-rate to bias sampling? That avoids burning through quota on short flurries.

li: Important: whatever we do, redact PII before any hashing/IDing. If we rely on hashed prompt fingerprints for deterministic sampling we must run the scrubber first. Hashing raw prompt text without deid = nope.

sam: Sketch config idea (pseudo):

```yaml
sampler:
  default: 0.02
  per_route:
    /v1/chat: 0.05
  burst_protection:
    window_sec: 60
    max_samples_per_window: 200
  cost_aware:
    token_ewma_alpha: 0.2
    token_threshold: 50 # lower prob if tokens >> threshold
```

frank: Console UX needs: per-route toggle + dry-run mode that shows projected sampled count and projected billing delta for the month before you flip it. Also an override button for SRE during incidents.

maya: nice, dry-run idea would help product owners not freak out.

alisha: Also add an emergency fallback: if 5xx rate > 1% for a route, temporarily capture 100% of sampled requests for a short TTL and flag for engineers. That gives us debug data without full-time capture.

jules: For deterministic sampling we can use `hash(user_id) % 100 < X` to keep stability across requests, but if user_id is PII we need to use a salt & KMS-managed hashing key. li's point about scrubber-first stands.

li: Exactly. Implementation note: do scrubber -> token_count -> hashing -> sampling decision. Keep audit logs of scrubber hits but not raw values.

sam: UX/ops API for temporary overrides (example):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/sampler/override \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/chat","dry_run":true,"max_samples":100,"window_sec":60}'
```

frank: We should also show a small forecast chart: sample_rate * expected_traffic -> expected_samples/day -> expected_cost. console can compute using historical traffic.

deploy-bot: Canary sampler config pushed to staging at 1750000005 by @jules :rocket:

maya: I'll draft an RFC with the config, UX mock, and a short rollout plan (staged: staging -> canary tenants -> org-wide). Will include canary metrics to watch: samples/sec, inspect_quota_remaining, token_cost_estimate.

sam: FYI we should include a migration plan for existing per-route rules so we don't double-count when burst protection is enabled.

alisha: +1 on migration plan. include an emergency kill-switch for the canary.

maya: cool, thanks everyone. I'll post the RFC this afternoon and ping for reviews. :thumbsup:
